issues.problem: This is the maintained legacy/Custom API host, not the root for IPinfo's current Lite, Core, Plus, and Max APIs.
issues.suggestion: Use https://api.ipinfo.io. For the current free API, use endpoints under /lite.

issues.problem: 50,000 requests/month describes the legacy free API. The current recommended IPinfo Lite plan allows unlimited authenticated API requests, with country-level geolocation and basic ASN data.
issues.suggestion: Set to "IPinfo Lite: unlimited authenticated requests; country-level geolocation and basic ASN data. Legacy Free API: 50,000 requests/month."

issues.problem: The listed self-serve tiers are outdated; the current lineup uses Max rather than Business.
issues.suggestion: Use "Core, Plus, Max, and Enterprise; see https://ipinfo.io/pricing".

issues.problem: The entry presents the legacy 50,000-request quota as the general free limit, omitting the unlimited current Lite plan.
issues.suggestion: Use "IPinfo Lite: unlimited authenticated requests; legacy free API: 50,000 requests/month; paid quotas vary by plan."

issues.problem: The curl and response use IPinfo's legacy endpoint and schema, while the entry is presented as the current general IPinfo API.
issues.suggestion: Either label the example explicitly as legacy or use curl "https://api.ipinfo.io/lite/8.8.8.8?token=YOUR_API_KEY" and provide a Lite-schema response.

issues.problem: The standard current free allowance is publicly stated as 1,000 lookups per month, rather than an unspecified limit that varies.
issues.suggestion: Set to "1,000 free lookups/month" and note that feature availability can depend on the lookup product.

issues.problem: The Proxy Detection API returns the ISP field as uppercase "ISP"; the snippet uses lowercase "isp", which is inconsistent with the documented interface.
The current Community plan permits 10,000 calls/month, not 5,000.
The stated 5,000-call quota is wrong, and the claim that paid per-minute limits are not publicly detailed is false.
The authoritative interactive documentation for the shown Search Foundation endpoint is hosted at api.jina.ai/docs.
issues.suggestion: Use https://api.jina.ai/docs for this API entry.

issues.problem: The free allowance is published rather than unknown. New users currently receive 10 million free tokens.
issues.suggestion: Set to "New users receive 10 million free tokens; usage and product-specific rate limits apply."

issues.problem: Jina publishes rate limits, so "not published" is incorrect. Limits also differ by product and tier.
issues.suggestion: Record product-specific limits. The current Search Foundation OpenAPI lists the Free tier at 500 RPM, 1 million TPM, and 5 concurrent requests; Reader and Search endpoints have separate limits.

issues.problem: The entry implies Reader and web Search are served from api.jina.ai, but those products use separate roots: r.jina.ai and s.jina.ai. DeepSearch also has its own host.
issues.suggestion: Limit this entry to the Search Foundation APIs on api.jina.ai, or explicitly list r.jina.ai, s.jina.ai, and deepsearch.jina.ai as separate product endpoints.

issues.problem: Rate limits are published in the project's documentation.
issues.suggestion: Set to "4 requests/second burst limit and 500 requests/hour sustained limit."

issues.problem: Jolpica requires clients to send a custom identifying User-Agent, but the curl example relies only on curl's generic default User-Agent.
The current endpoint now returns the 2026 season, while the fixed response snippet says 2025.
issues.suggestion: Refresh the snippet to the current response or avoid hard-coding the season for a /current endpoint.

issues.problem: The entry conflates Kaggle's current API token with its legacy username/key credentials. Current tokens use OAuth/Bearer-style authentication; username plus key in kaggle.json is explicitly the legacy option.
issues.suggestion: Describe current authentication as OAuth or an API token sent as a Bearer token. Mention username/key Basic Auth and kaggle.json only as legacy authentication generated through "Create Legacy API Key."

issues.problem: The Basic Auth example works only with legacy username/key credentials, but it labels the password as the general current API key and the auth instructions direct users toward the newer token flow.
issues.suggestion: Prefer curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" "https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/list?search=titanic", or explicitly label the existing curl as requiring a legacy API key.
